1219. ἐλειονόμοι: those that dwell in marshes. LgP

1220. Ἀμαραντίου: The Amarantii are a barbarian tribe beyond the Colchians on the mainland, from where the sources of the Phasis burst forth. Or a Colchian mountain called Amarantion, from which the Phasis flows down.
4 1197. Et. Gen. (AB) κλωπήιος: κλεπτικός. III 1197. Ἀπολλώνιος.

1226. θώρηκα στάδιον: because it was not chain-mail, but a standing corselet; it is formed from 'standing'. But some say 'στάδιον' means well-made, which Callimachus also says (fg 59 Schn. = 145 Kapp): 'and he wore a well-made tunic'.

1240. οἷος δ’ Ἴσθμιον: The Isthmian games are those celebrated at the Isthmus of Corinth, formerly in honor of Poseidon, but later in honor of Melicertes at the command of the then king Sisyphus son of Aeolus; when he saw the body of Melicertes washed ashore at Corinth, he recognized that it was his nephew, the son of Athamas son of Aeolus, and honored him, as was fitting, also with the Isthmian contest, in which the victors were crowned with pine in old times, but later with dry celery. But Musaeus in his work On the Isthmian Games (M. IV 518) says that two contests take place at the Isthmus, one of Poseidon and one of Melicertes.
11 Hyp. Pind. Isthm. a—d sch. Eur. Med. 1284 Paus. I 44, 8. II 1, 3 Apoll. Bibl. III 29 Hyg. Fab. 2 Clem. Al. Protr. II 34, 1 Tzetz. Lyc. 56, 5. 104, 18 Sch.
1241. ἢ Ταίναρον: Taenarum is a promontory of Laconia. Lerna is a spring of Argos sacred to Poseidon: 'surpassing hierophant of the Lernaian sanctuaries' (Anth. Pal. IX 688, 4).
